description: A meat processing plant uses two machines, a meat slicer and a meat packer, to make their hams and pork ribs. To produce one batch of hams requires 4 hours on the meat slicer and 2.5 hours on the meat packer. To produce one batch of pork ribs requires 2 hours on the meat slicer and 3.5 hours on the meat packer. Each machine runs for at most 4000 hours per year. If the profit per batch of hams is $150 and the profit per batch of pork ribs is $300, how many batches of each should be made to maximize profit?

ProfitPerBatch.definition: Profit per batch of each product

TimeRequired.definition: Time required on each machine to produce one batch of each product

MaxHours.definition: Maximum available hours per year for each machine

objective.description: "Maximize the total profit from producing batches of hams and pork ribs"

constraints.description: 4 hours times the number of ham batches plus 2 hours times the number of pork rib batches should not exceed 4000 hours (meat slicer time constraint)
2.5 hours times the number of ham batches plus 3.5 hours times the number of pork rib batches should not exceed 4000 hours (meat packer time constraint)
The number of ham batches and the number of pork rib batches produced must be non-negative
